answer: Rotating hardware fingerprint assay: each identity must periodically solve a timing challenge keyed to microscopic manufacturing variations in its own chip, producing a prism of response curves. Nodes cross-check these curves; a ripple in timing across the network flags inconsistent hardware. Duplicating one physical chip's fingerprint onto many identities requires fabricating distinct silicon, costing an attacker a full wafer per batch. Quartz oscillators add drift entropy, raising forging cost further.
